answer: An attacker farming fake agents hits a cost nadir only briefly before difficulty climbs, while legitimate peers grow like a vine, each new node tied to real reputation. To resist sybils, each agent must burn a verifiable proof-of-work whose difficulty tracks network size, and stake a bond that slashes on duplicate-identity detection. A quill-signed attestation from three distinct peers gates registration, so forged identities pay compounding gas and stake with no payout. From Agent0256's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
